## Textbooks

**An Introduction to Statistical Learning** — James, Witten, Hastie, Tibshirani (2021, Springer).
The spine of the course. Chapters 3, 4, 6, 8, 10 and 12 map almost one-to-one onto our lectures.
[Free PDF + labs →](https://www.statlearning.com/)

**Data Science for Business** — Provost & Fawcett (2013, O'Reilly).
Read this one for *why*, not for *how*. Best source on framing a business problem as a data problem, and on what a model is actually worth to a firm.

**Practical Time Series Forecasting with R** — Shmueli & Polak (2024, Axelrod Schnall).
Companion for the Module 1 forecasting block.

Additional readings and support material: [Blackboard]({{< var blackboard-url >}}).

## Materials on Blackboard

Two folders are open on [Blackboard]({{< var blackboard-url >}}), one per module.

They are **visible but empty for the moment** — deliberately so, so that you can
find them and check they are there before there is anything to download. Prof.
Arbia's material fills the Module 1 folder and Prof. Salvini's the Module 2
folder, posted as each block runs rather than all at once.

Slides, code and datasets linked from the [schedule](index.qmd) are the same
files you will find in those folders. Nothing is published in one place only.

## Going deeper

Optional. None of this is examinable — it is here for when a topic catches you.

**Regularisation and high-dimensional data**
: *Statistical Learning with Sparsity* — Hastie, Tibshirani, Wainwright. [Free PDF](https://hastie.su.domains/StatLearnSparsity/)

**Forecasting**
: *Forecasting: Principles and Practice* (3rd ed.) — Hyndman & Athanasopoulos. [Free online](https://otexts.com/fpp3/) — the reference for `fable`.

**Model interpretability**
: *Interpretable Machine Learning* — Christoph Molnar. [Free online](https://christophm.github.io/interpretable-ml-book/) — SHAP, LIME, partial dependence, done properly.

**Data visualization**
: *Fundamentals of Data Visualization* — Claus Wilke. [Free online](https://clauswilke.com/dataviz/)
: *The Visual Display of Quantitative Information* — Tufte. Buy it on paper.

**Generative AI in the analytics workflow**
: Use it. Then check it. A model that writes `glmnet` code will also confidently write `glmnet` code that standardises the wrong matrix — the exam asks you to read code, not to have generated it.
